fullPassage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals—sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.

✅ ① complex: complex(복잡한)는 simple(단순한)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ② easy: easy(쉬운)는 simple과 유사한 의미
❌ ③ plain: plain(간단한/평범한)은 simple과 유사한 의미
❌ ④ basic: basic(기본적인)은 simple과 유사한 의미
det.tip: simple(단순한) ↔ complex(복잡한)

questions.passage:
(A) Aristotle missed the <u>sense</u> of balance, which has links to both touch and vision in the human body.
(B) What you just said does not make much <u>sense</u> to me, so could you please explain it again?
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 sense의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: sense: (A) (명사) 감각 / (B) (명사) 의미/타당성 (make sense)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 의미/타당성 — (B) 감각: (A)의 sense는 'sense of balance(균형 감각)'의 감각이지 의미가 아님
✅ ② (A) 감각 — (B) 의미/타당성: (A)는 'the sense of balance(균형 감각)', (B)는 'make sense(타당하다/말이 되다)'로 다의어의 두 쓰임을 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 감각 — (B) 방향: (B)의 sense는 방향이 아닌 '의미/타당성'
❌ ④ (A) 분별력 — (B) 의미: (A)는 분별력이 아닌 '감각'
det.tip: sense: ① (명사) 감각 ② make sense (의미가 통하다/타당하다)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal"

det.korean: prey=먹잇감 (다른 동물에게 사냥되어 먹히는 동물)
det.analysis:
❌ ① odor(냄새): 사냥 대상이 아니라 후각으로 탐지되는 것
❌ ② vision(시각): 감각의 하나로 동물이 아님
❌ ③ balance(균형): 감각의 하나로 동물이 아님
✅ ④ prey: prey(먹잇감)는 '다른 동물에게 사냥되어 먹히는 동물'이라는 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: prey = 먹잇감 (hunted and eaten by another animal)

questions.passage: These examples tell us that senses cannot be clearly __________ (divide) into a limited number of specific kinds. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 조동사 뒤 수동태(be + p.p.)이므로 과거분사 divided
det.analysis: 'senses cannot be clearly ___ into'에서 cannot be 뒤에 수동태의 과거분사가 와야 한다. 감각이 '나뉘는' 수동이므로 divide → divided가 적절하다.
det.tip: 조동사 + be + p.p. (수동태): cannot be divided

questions.passage: Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle __________ (write) that there are five senses, in both humans and animals. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 약 2,370년 전의 일이므로 과거시제. write의 불규칙 과거형 wrote
det.analysis: 'Around 2,370 years ago(약 2,370년 전)'라는 과거 시점이 있으므로 과거시제가 필요하다. write는 불규칙 동사로 과거형이 wrote이다. write → wrote → written
det.tip: 불규칙 과거: write → wrote (과거 시점 2,370 years ago)

questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals—sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even __________. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: harder to categorize=분류하기 더 어려운 — 다른 동물의 감각은 분류하기 훨씬 더 어렵다는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① harder to categorize(분류하기 더 어려운): 'Other animals have senses that are even ___'에서 뒤이어 척추동물의 후각 체계, 뱀의 체열 감지 등 분류가 어려운 예가 나오므로 부합 ←정답
❌ ② easy to explain(설명하기 쉬운): 분류의 어려움을 드는 예시와 반대
❌ ③ simple to count(세기 간단한): 뒤의 예시와 모순
❌ ④ quick to learn(빨리 배우는): 감각 분류의 어려움과 무관
det.tip: senses that are even harder to categorize — 분류하기 더 어려운 감각들

questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals—sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses __________ into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: cannot be clearly divided=명확하게 나뉠 수 없다 — 감각이 제한된 수의 특정 종류로 명확히 나뉘지 않는다는 맥락
det.analysis:
❌ ① must be strictly counted(엄격히 세어야 한다): 명확한 분류가 불가능하다는 글의 논지와 반대
✅ ② cannot be clearly divided(명확하게 나뉠 수 없다): 'senses ___ into a limited number of specific kinds'에서 감각이 제한된 수의 특정 종류로 명확히 나뉠 수 없다는 맥퍼슨의 주장에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ should be fully ignored(완전히 무시되어야 한다): 본문 주장과 무관
❌ ④ will be easily combined(쉽게 결합될 것이다): 분류 불가를 말하는 맥락과 다름
det.tip: senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds
